result: On polysomnography 58% of CFS patients had a previously undiagnosed primary sleep disorder (sleep apnoea/hypopnoea, restless legs/periodic limb movements), with high self-reported insomnia and non-restorative sleep; psychological maladjustment was similar to narcolepsy patients.
reason: Same measure (PSG), but finding a high rate of clinical sleep disorders goes against the claim that PSG usually finds no explanatory disorder; not cited

result: In 14 female CFS patients vs 14 controls, a 2-min sustained biceps MVC with endplate stimulation showed lower MVC and larger central activation failure (36.5% vs 12.9%), with less peripheral fatigue and normal stimulated force at rest.
reason: Sustained biceps MVC with twitch interpolation measures central drive, matching the central motor-fatigability finding rather than repeated handgrip decline/recovery

result: In 20 MZ twin pairs discordant for CFS, CFS twins reported more sleepiness (ESS 10.9 vs 8.2, p=.03; SSS 3.4 vs 2.1), but MSLT mean sleep latencies were similar and non-pathological.
reason: Objective sleep testing (MSLT) in a co-twin design finds no pathological sleepiness, supporting the no-explanatory-disorder part of the finding

result: In 21 MZ twin pairs discordant for CFS plus 21 controls, CFS twins did not differ from healthy co-twins on any of 10 tests; both twin groups were slower than unrelated controls on speed-dependent tests except finger tapping.
reason: Same measures (processing speed); no case vs co-twin difference contradicts a disease-linked deficit, suggesting a shared familial trait

result: 141 Fukuda CFS patients vs 76 controls scored at least 1 SD below the control mean on 9 of 18 measures and 2 SD below on 4, and failed more often in attention, processing speed and motor speed but not memory or executive function.
reason: Independent cohort, same domains, same direction (attention and processing speed deficits)

result: 56 CFS patients vs 35 healthy volunteers sampled at 0-60 min after waking had a lower salivary cortisol awakening response (AUC).
reason: Same measure (salivary awakening cortisol), same direction; not among cited studies

result: Two-night PSG in 22 MZ twin pairs discordant for CFS showed a higher percentage of stage 3 and REM sleep in CFS twins, with no major architecture abnormality and some respiratory impairment that could not explain the sleep complaints.
reason: Same measure (PSG); a co-twin design consistent with more N3 and no explanatory disorder

result: Review of the authors' work: tilt-derived hemodynamic instability score (HIS > -0.98; sens 84.5%, spec 85.1%) and fractal score (FRAS > +0.22; sens 70%, spec 88%) identified CFS, and an uncontrolled midodrine pilot reported correction of dysautonomia followed by less fatigue.
reason: Does not measure resting HR or HF-HRV; the only testable link is the uncontrolled midodrine pilot in CFS, which adds to the midodrine finding that no outcome trial exists

result: In 19 CFS vs 11 sedentary controls, gastrocnemius 31P-MRS PCr recovery and post-exercise hyperaemic flow were normal; with partial cuff occlusion CFS had lower hyperaemic flow (p<0.01) and slower O2 saturation recovery (p<0.05), but the same drop in oxidative metabolism.
reason: An MRS study finding no group muscle metabolic abnormality, adding to the null side; it reports PCr recovery rather than pH, so weak

result: In 65 population-identified Wichita CFS cases followed up to 3 years, only 20-33% still met CFS criteria at follow-up, 56.9% ever had partial or total remission, 10% sustained total remission and 23.1% got alternative diagnoses; shorter illness duration predicted sustained remission.
reason: Same outcome (remission/recovery); sustained total remission of 10% falls within the reviewed 0-31% range, in a population-based sample
